title: Reconciling Free Will and Divine Decree
paragraphs: After years avoiding a philosophical question that had quietly troubled him since university, Faris finally sought out a scholar to discuss how personal responsibility could coexist meaningfully with belief in Allah's complete foreknowledge of every future event.

The scholar explained that this apparent tension had occupied serious theological attention for centuries, with the mainstream position holding that Allah's knowledge of outcomes does not eliminate genuine human choice in reaching them.

Rather than fully resolving every philosophical dimension of the question, an ambition the scholar suggested exceeded what human reasoning alone could definitively achieve, the conversation helped Faris hold both convictions simultaneously without experiencing them as contradictory.

This resolution, while intellectually incomplete by the strictest philosophical standards, provided Faris genuine practical peace, illustrating that some theological questions benefit from workable understanding rather than requiring complete logical resolution before acceptance.
